summary: Describes IS-IS extensions that support IEEE 802.1aq Shortest Path Bridging, which provides true shortest-path forwarding across equal-cost paths in mesh Ethernet networks. It allows much larger Layer 2 topologies with faster convergence and better use of the mesh.

eli5.summary: Normal Ethernet networks use only part of their cables to avoid loops. This lets switches find the quickest route and use many cables at once, so big networks work faster.

questions: what is the difference between spbm and spbv
subtitle: How IS-IS was extended with a handful of TLVs so Ethernet bridges can compute shortest paths and use the whole mesh.

tldr.problem: Spanning-tree style Ethernet bridging limits how large a Layer 2 network can grow and leaves much of a mesh unused. IEEE 802.1aq Shortest Path Bridging (SPB) needs a control protocol to compute shortest paths.
tldr.mechanism: IS-IS, with a new NLPID (0xC1) and a small set of new TLVs and sub-TLVs, advertises SPB capabilities, VLAN usage, link metrics and service membership. Each bridge uses this to fill its forwarding tables from the IS-IS database.
tldr.outcome: SPB gets true shortest-path forwarding over multiple equal-cost paths, larger Layer 2 topologies and faster convergence, with no state machine changes to IS-IS itself.

today: RFC 6329 is a Proposed Standard published in April 2012, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It documents the IS-IS side of 802.1aq; the IEEE standard remains the definitive source for the bridging behavior.

sections.title: IS-IS as the Control Protocol for 802.1aq
sections.content:
IEEE 802.1aq Shortest Path Bridging (SPB) is described as the next step in the evolution of the various spanning tree and registration protocols. It allows true shortest-path forwarding in an Ethernet mesh using multiple equal-cost paths, which supports much larger Layer 2 topologies, faster convergence and better use of the mesh. It also offers single-point provisioning of logical connectivity: point-to-point (E-LINE), point-to-multipoint (E-TREE) and multipoint-to-multipoint (E-LAN).

The control protocol is IS-IS augmented with a small number of TLVs and sub-TLVs. It supports two Ethernet encapsulating data paths: 802.1ad Provider Bridges (Q-in-Q) and 802.1ah Provider Backbone Bridges (MAC-in-MAC). This RFC documents the TLVs and gives some overview.

802.1aq needs no state machine or other substantive change to IS-IS. It only needs a new Network Layer Protocol Identifier (NLPID) and the new TLVs. If this memo and the IS-IS standard disagree, IS-IS is authoritative.
sections.eli5: Switches already have a language for sharing maps of the network. This RFC adds a few new words to that language so they can share what Ethernet needs.

sections.title: The Two Modes: SPBM and SPBV
sections.content:
802.1aq has two modes. In SPBV (SPB VID), multiple VLANs can spread load over different shortest-path trees, each computed with a different tie-breaking rule. In SPBM (SPB MAC), service instances are identified by I-SIDs, and VLANs can again spread load over different trees. SPBM is used with 802.1ah encapsulation; SPBV can be used with VLANs, Provider Bridges or Provider Backbone Bridges. The two modes can co-exist in one SPB network. The practical design goals in the current 802.1aq specification are networks of 100 nodes for SPBV and 1000 nodes for SPBM.

In both modes, routes are shortest-path, symmetric between any source and destination in the domain, and congruent for unicast and multicast. That means the shortest path tree to a node matches the multicast distribution tree from it. Symmetry and congruency preserve packet ordering and keep OAM flows on the same path as the traffic, so existing 802.1ag and Y.1731 OAM mechanisms work.

Because a single tree could leave links under-used, different deterministic tie-breakers allow up to 16 shortest paths of arbitrary diversity between any pair of nodes, spreading traffic on a VLAN basis.

SPB also uses IS-IS Multi-Topology (MT) so that several logical SPB instances can live in one IS-IS instance, each tied to an MT ID. VLANs MUST NOT overlap between SPB instances. Using MT IDs other than the default 0 is optional.

The overview section of the RFC is explicitly informative. For definitive behavior it points to the IEEE 802.1aq standard.
sections.eli5: There are two ways to label the roads: by a tag on each car (SPBV) or by a full delivery address on a box (SPBM). Both let the traffic lights pick the shortest route and share the load across several routes.

sections.title: How Frames Are Forwarded
sections.content:
In SPBM unicast, frames are wrapped in an 802.1ah header with a Backbone Source Address (B-SA), Backbone Destination Address (B-DA), Backbone VLAN ID (B-VID) and an I-Component Service Instance ID. On intermediate (tandem) nodes the B-DA is forwarded without learning: the forwarding database (FDB) entries mapping a B-DA and B-VID to an outgoing interface come only from the IS-IS database and its computations. Tandem nodes also run an ingress check. If the B-SA and B-VID, looked up as a destination, do not point to the arrival port, the frame is discarded. The RFC calls this a very powerful loop mitigation mechanism.

For SPBM multicast there are two choices. With head-end replication, the ingress node copies the frame once per receiver and sends each copy as unicast, so the core needs no multicast state. It is for sparse groups or little multicast traffic, and the node must not advertise the I-SID with the Transmit (T) bit set. With tandem replication, the shortest path tree is used and frames are copied only where the tree forks. It saves bandwidth but needs multicast FDB entries in core bridges, and it is triggered when the I-SID is advertised with the T bit set.

The multicast destination address concatenates a 20-bit SPSourceID (a nodal identifier) with the 24-bit I-SID, so it uniquely identifies the source and group tree. The I-SID value 0xfff is reserved for SPBM control traffic.

In SPBV, the ingress bridge translates VLAN IDs to the per-source SPVID. The SPVID is unidirectional, so shared VLAN learning is used between the forward and reverse SPVIDs of one Base VID, and unicast MACs are learned as in normal bridging. Multicast MAC addresses can be configured or learned through MMRP, which ends at the SPBV edge while IS-IS carries the addresses.
sections.eli5: Switches in the middle do not guess where to send things. They follow a map built from the shared network information, and they throw away any frame that shows up from a direction it should not come from.

sections.title: Tie-Breaking and Equal Cost Trees
sections.content:
Two rules keep shortest-path results symmetric and deterministic. First, if the two ends of a link advertise different SPB link metrics, calculations MUST use the maximum of the two. Second, when two paths have equal total metrics, the one with the fewest hops between the fork and join points MUST win. If hop counts also match, the path through the intermediate node with the lower BridgeID MUST be chosen. The BridgeID is 8 bytes: a 2-byte BridgePriority followed by the 6-byte SYSID. An operator can steer the choice by raising a node's Bridge Priority.

The default algorithm is ECT-Algorithm 00-80-c2-01. To create diversity, SPB defines 16 variations with worldwide unique IDs 00-80-C2-01 through 00-80-C2-10, made of the IEEE 802.1 OUI 00-80-C2 plus an index. Each variation picks the path with the lowest value of the BridgeID XORed byte by byte with an ECT-MASK. Mask 1 is all zeros, which gives the default; mask 2 inverts the BridgeID so the largest ID wins. ECT-ALGORITHMs are mapped to VIDs and services are assigned to those VIDs, giving a degree of traffic engineering.

Two opaque ECT TLVs let future algorithms carry their own parameters.
sections.eli5: When two routes are equally good, the switches need a rule so they all pick the same one. They compare their ID numbers. Mixing up the rule a few ways lets different traffic take different routes.

sections.title: Hello (IIH) Extensions
sections.content:
SPB can run beside IPv4 and IPv6, so failing to form an SPB adjacency MUST NOT cause rejection of the adjacency for other network layer protocols. SPBs MUST use the NLPID 0xC1 in the IIH Protocols Supported TLV (type 129). 802.1aq frames MUST flow only on adjacencies that advertise this NLPID in both directions, and otherwise the adjacency counts as nonexistent with an infinite metric. IS-IS for SPB supports only point-to-point adjacencies and MUST use the three-way handshake of RFC 5303; pseudonodes are avoided.

The hello carries three new sub-TLVs inside the MT-Port-Cap TLV:

  • SPB-MCID (type 4): two 51-byte MCIDs from IEEE 802.1Q, a digest of which VIDs run which control protocols. It MUST be the same on all bridges in an SPT Region. The second (aux) MCID allows migration without interrupting traffic.
  • SPB-Digest (type 5, optional): an Agreement Digest over all SPB adjacencies, with a 2-bit Agreement Number and Discarded Agreement Number. While digests disagree, unsafe multicast forwarding is blocked for trees whose root distance changed. If supported, it MUST be sent on every hello, and if only one peer supports it, neither side does digest-based loop prevention.
  • SPB-B-VID (type 6): a list of 6-byte ECT-VID tuples, each with a 32-bit ECT-ALGORITHM, a 12-bit Base VID, a Use flag (U) and an M bit (1 for SPBM, 0 for SPBV).
sections.eli5: When two neighbors say hello, they also show each other a short summary of their settings, so they can tell right away if they disagree about how the roads are set up.

sections.title: Node, Link and Service Information
sections.content:
The LSP-level information travels in a new MT-Capability TLV (type 144) and in the existing adjacency TLVs.

  • SPB-Inst (sub-TLV 1): carries the 20-bit SPSourceID, Bridge Priority, CIST root information for interworking with RSTP and MSTP, and one tuple per ECT-ALGORITHM and Base VID with the SPVID for SPBV. It MUST be in the fragment zero LSP and MUST list at least ECT-ALGORITHM 00-80-C2-01. SPSourceIDs and SPVIDs may be auto-allocated, and the highest Bridge Identifier wins a clash.
  • SPB-Metric (sub-TLV 29): a 24-bit unsigned link cost, one per SPB instance per link, in the MT-ISN TLV (222) or Extended IS Reachability TLV (22). Without it, the adjacency MUST NOT carry SPB traffic. The maximum value 2^24 - 1 means the link must not carry SPB traffic because incompatible SPB parameters were found.
  • SPBM-SI (sub-TLV 3): a B-MAC address and a list of I-SIDs, each with a T and an R bit saying whether the node transmits, receives or both.
  • SPBV-ADDR (sub-TLV 4): group MAC addresses for SPBV, with T and R bits, replacing MMRP for the shortest-path trees.
  • Opaque ECT-ALGORITHM sub-TLVs (types 2 and 30) hold parameters for future algorithms.

For IANA, the NLPID 0xC1 was already assigned. This RFC adds sub-TLVs under the MT-Port-Cap TLV (143), the new MT-Capability TLV (144) and the MT-ISN TLV (222). Type 144 gets a new sub-registry starting at sub-TLV value 1, managed by Expert Review.
sections.eli5: Each switch shares a card with its ID, which roads it uses, how costly each road is, and which groups it wants to join.

sections.title: Worked Examples on a 7-Node Network
sections.content:
The RFC uses a 7-node network (nodes :1 to :7, B-MACs 4455-6677-00xx) with the default ECT-ALGORITHM mapped to B-VID 100 and all links at equal cost. Node :1 transmits and receives I-SID 1, as do nodes :3, :5 and :7. Node :1's unicast entries send traffic for :3, :5 and :7 out interface 2, while its direct neighbors use their own links. It has one multicast entry for its own tree, because it is not a transit node.

Node :2 is the center and has a direct path to every other node. As a transit node for the four members of I-SID 1, it needs four multicast entries, one per source tree. The entry for node :1's tree arrives on interface 1 and replicates out interfaces 2, 3 and 5 to reach :3, :5 and :7.

For SPBV, the SPVID is the Base VID plus the node ID (101 to 107 for Base VID 100). Node :2 forwards by SPVID, with wild-card destination addresses and shared VLAN learning, and adds separate entries for the multicast group address 0300-0000-000f.
sections.eli5: The examples show one small town with seven crossroads and how the center crossroad ends up with a different set of signposts for each starting point.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC states that it adds no new security risks to IS-IS, and no extra security either, when used in a configured environment or a single-operator domain such as a data center.

It may also be used in zero-configuration environments, where network-to-network ports (NNIs) and user ports (UNIs) form automatically. There are then intrinsic concerns that should be mitigated with authentication procedures, which are beyond the scope of the document and yet to be defined. Setting the T bit on an I-SID can create large amounts of multicast state, so extra care is needed to prevent denial-of-service abuse (see RFC 4732) in zero-configuration setups.
sections.eli5: If switches join the network on their own without any password, a bad one could join and cause trouble, so extra care is needed there.
